hints: Remember stereoisomers here means both types, so look for E/Z isomerism around the C=C and optical isomerism at any chiral centre.
Check the C=C first. Three of these alkenes can show E/Z, but one has two identical methyl groups on the same double-bond carbon so it cannot.
Now look for a carbon with four different groups. Only one molecule has both E/Z and a chiral centre, so multiply 2 by 2 to get its total.
walkthrough:
**Recall the two sources of stereoisomerism**

Great start. For alkenes we count geometric (E/Z) isomers and optical isomers separately.

Total stereoisomers = (number from E/Z) x (number from chiral centres)

**Test for E/Z isomerism**

E/Z is possible only if each C of the C=C has two different groups.

$\text{C2}$ in 2-methylhex-2-ene is $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}=$, so it has two identical $\text{CH}_3$ groups. No E/Z there, only 1 form.

The other three, 3-methyl, 4-methyl and 5-methylhex-2-ene, all have $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CH}-$, with H and carbon groups different on each end. Each gives 2 geometric isomers, E and Z.

**Test for a chiral centre**

A chiral centre is a saturated carbon with four different groups, giving a pair of enantiomers.

Draw 4-methylhex-2-ene: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$

Carbon 4 is bonded to H, $\text{CH}_3$, $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, and $\text{CH}=\text{CHCH}_3$. All four are different, so C4 is chiral.

**Count and compare**

For 4-methylhex-2-ene we have 2 from E/Z and 2 from optical (R and S).

$$\text{total} = 2 \times 2 = 4 \text{ stereoisomers}$$

The others have either no E/Z and no chiral centre (1 total) or E/Z only (2 total). So 4-methylhex-2-ene has the greatest number.

options.A: Incorrect. 2-methylhex-2-ene is $(CH_3)_2C=CHCH_2CH_2CH_3$. C2 has two identical methyl groups so no E/Z isomerism is possible, and there is no chiral centre. It has only 1 stereoisomer.
options.B: Incorrect. 3-methylhex-2-ene is $CH_3CH=C(CH_3)CH_2CH_2CH_3$. It shows E/Z isomerism (2 forms) because both C2 and C3 have two different groups, but it has no carbon with four different groups, so no optical isomers. Total is 2.
options.C: Correct. 4-methylhex-2-ene is $CH_3CH=CHCH(CH_3)CH_2CH_3$. It shows E/Z isomerism (2 forms) and C4 is chiral with H, CH3, CH2CH3 and CH=CHCH3 attached (2 enantiomers). Total is 2 x 2 = 4 stereoisomers, the largest in the list.
options.D: Incorrect. 5-methylhex-2-ene is $CH_3CH=CHCH_2CH(CH_3)_2$. It shows E/Z isomerism (2 forms), but C5 is $CH(CH_3)_2$ with two identical methyl groups so it is not chiral. Total is 2.
